ex08.title: Bitcoin ETF explained: what you own and what you don't
ex08.reel_caption:
Bitcoin ETF explained: you get the price, not the keys. 🔑

A spot Bitcoin ETF is a fund you buy like a share. The catch: a yearly fee, trading only in market hours, and you can't send that Bitcoin anywhere. Simplicity or control, and the price can still drop hard either way.

next-collapse.title: Are we closer to the next financial collapse? 5 warning lights are on
next-collapse.reel_caption:
Are we closer to the next financial collapse? 🚨

Before 2000, 2008 and 2020, the same warning lights came on first. I checked them against today:

🔴 Top 10 companies = ~40% of the S&P 500 (2000: ~25%)
🔴 Margin debt near a record $1.5T, now rolling over
🔴 Riskiest company debt cracking (only seen in 2000, 2008, 2016, 2020)
🔴 Chip stocks −12% in one day (5 Nov)
🔴 Bitcoin ~40% off its high, ETF money leaving
⚪ Still missing: jobs breaking, a big lender failing

My view: this looks more like 2000 than 2008. Date to watch: 30 Nov.

next-collapse.li_text:
Are we closer to the next financial collapse?

Before 2000, 2008 and 2020, the same warning lights came on first. I checked 15 of them against today: 5 are on, 7 are flickering, 3 are off.

What's on:
→ The 10 biggest companies are ~40% of the S&P 500. At the 2000 peak it was ~25%.
→ Margin debt hit a record ~$1.5T and is starting to roll over, as it did before 2000 and 2007.
→ The riskiest company debt (CCC) is cracking. That gap has only been this wide in 2000, 2008, 2016 and 2020.
→ Chip stocks fell 12% in one day on 5 Nov.
→ Bitcoin is ~40% off its high, and ETF money is leaving.

What's missing: in every past crash, jobs broke and a big lender failed. Neither has happened. Yet.

My view: this looks more like 2000 than 2008. I'm watching junk-bond spreads, the dollar and jobless claims, and 30 Nov, when Trump Media's $1B notes can be called.

My opinion, not financial advice. Data as of 7 Nov 2026.

Which warning light are you watching?

#markets #investing #economy
